solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Field study for second degree (6)

blocks.note: to do a subject is to study it
a Master of Arts, the degree after a BA
the subject you take a degree for is the one it is in

annotation.surface: Someone choosing fieldwork as the research for a master's.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a phrase: to 'do an MA in' history is to study for a second degree.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: your field of expertise is your domain, the area you rule over.

entries.clue: Levant PM unable to contact service to north (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards

blocks.note: a player who is aced cannot get a racket to the serve

annotation.surface: A Middle Eastern prime minister cut off from the military, somewhere to the north.
annotation.walkthrough: Levant looks like the eastern Mediterranean region, but it is a verb here: to levant is to run off leaving debts unpaid. The service is a tennis serve, not the armed forces.
annotation.definitionFit: To levant and to decamp both mean to leave suddenly or secretly.

entries.clue: Million nuts that must be shelled tomorrow (6)

indicators.note: shelling removes the outer layer, here the first and last letters

blocks.note: BANANAS (nuts, mad) without its outer letters

annotation.surface: A huge order of nuts whose shells have to come off by tomorrow.
annotation.walkthrough: The nuts are not something to crack: 'bananas' means crazy, and it is the word that gets shelled.
annotation.definitionFit: Mañana is Spanish for tomorrow, used in English for putting things off.

entries.clue: Very soon desert old lover (9)

blocks.note: to rat is to desert your side

annotation.surface: A warning that you are about to walk out on a former partner.
annotation.walkthrough: Desert is a verb, not sand. 'In a mo' is British slang for 'in a moment'.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary loan from Italian, where the word means 'enamoured', applied to a man in love.

entries.clue: Mince on side of skewers almost resembling kebab (8)

indicators.note: in an across clue, HASH sits on (after) S
the side of a word is its edge, here the first letter
almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short of its end

annotation.surface: Minced meat pushed onto skewers until it looks like a kebab.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue sits in the kitchen, so kebab reads as part of the recipe rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Shashlik is a kebab of meat grilled on a skewer.

entries.clue: Weed covering allotment alas, mown regularly for war hero (7,6)

indicators.note: something covering another lies over it on both sides, so one word wraps round the other
at regular intervals, so only every second letter is kept

blocks.note: a ration is an allotted share

annotation.surface: A gardener lamenting weeds overrunning an allotment that is only mown now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: An allotment in Britain is a rented garden plot, which is what the surface wants, but here it means a ration.
annotation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was the British admiral who won at Trafalgar.

entries.clue: Back in Wetherspoons, groom curtailed binge (5)

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter
cut off at the tail: drop the last letter

annotation.surface: A bridegroom cut short in a cheap pub during a drinking session.
annotation.walkthrough: Wetherspoons is a chain of cheap British pubs. Groom is the verb, to preen, not a bridegroom.
annotation.definitionFit: A spree is a spell of unrestrained indulgence, like a binge.

entries.clue: Favour one side on march — without good reason, clearly (8)

blocks.note: a limp favours one leg while walking

annotation.surface: A political side-taking on a protest march, done for no clear reason.
annotation.walkthrough: The march is a walk, and favouring one side is what an injured walker does.
annotation.definitionFit: Limpidly means in a clear, transparent way.

entries.clue: Alarming colour after nap exercise class cured (8)

indicators.note: RED comes after KIP and PE

blocks.note: kip is British slang for a sleep
red is the colour of alarms

annotation.surface: Someone flushed a worrying colour after dozing, until an exercise class put them right.
annotation.walkthrough: Cured looks like 'healed', but it means preserved: a kipper is a smoked herring.
annotation.definitionFit: Kippered fish has been cured by salting and smoking.

entries.clue: Bottle among others set out near tonic (9)

indicators.note: the letters are laid out afresh

annotation.surface: A bottle placed with others next to the tonic water at a bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Among others' makes the definition fair: a bottle is just one of many kinds of container.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, made honest by 'among others', since a bottle is only one kind.

entries.clue: Often I meet Rob running rather late (3,6,4)

indicators.note: the letters are set in motion

annotation.surface: Someone who keeps bumping into Rob when he is jogging, a bit behind schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: Rob looks like a verb, which hides that it is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Not before time' is said of something that has come rather late.

entries.clue: Quiet American turned chart over (5)

indicators.note: turned round: read backwards

annotation.surface: The Quiet American, Graham Greene's novel, spun round on a chart.
annotation.walkthrough: The Quiet American is a Graham Greene novel, which glues the first two words together; they must be split.
annotation.definitionFit: RE- means again and 'over' means again, so charting over is mapping anew.

entries.clue: Gold miners brought round mountain (5)

indicators.note: turned round: read backwards

blocks.note: the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union

annotation.surface: Gold miners hauling their find round a mountain.
annotation.walkthrough: A Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet.
annotation.definitionFit: A Munro is a Scottish mountain higher than 3,000 feet.

entries.clue: Let out of wrong toilet, he left — just as she appeared (2,3,4)

indicators.note: the letters are put wrong
to be let out of somewhere is to leave it, so the letters L-E-T leave the word

annotation.surface: A man let out of the wrong toilet, leaving just as a woman walked in.
annotation.walkthrough: The opening 'Let out of' belongs to 'left', at the far end of the wordplay, leaving only F.
annotation.definitionFit: A portrait done to the life shows the sitter exactly as she appeared.

entries.clue: French teacher had me explain the merits of English (12)

blocks.note: had me do it = made me do it
to sell an idea is to explain its merits

annotation.surface: A pupil made to justify the value of English to their French teacher.
annotation.walkthrough: In British schools a female French teacher was traditionally addressed as Mademoiselle. 'French' does double duty, also putting 'me' into French.
annotation.definitionFit: Mademoiselle is how pupils addressed a woman teaching them French.

entries.clue: Well, well — divorced by British rugby player (9)

indicators.note: the two words are split apart by B

annotation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that a British rugby player has divorced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Well, well' reads as one exclamation but gives two different meanings, a noun and an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: The Springboks are South Africa's national rugby team.

entries.clue: Racer with ordinary history shares concern, failing to finish (5,3)

indicators.note: a word that fails to finish never reaches its end, so it loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A racing driver with an unremarkable past who is worried about not finishing.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because a stock car started life as an ordinary production car before being modified for racing.
annotation.definitionFit: A stock car is a standard production car adapted for racing.

entries.clue: Guerrillas struggle against leaders in the guard house (8)

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following words
T and G house CON between them

blocks.note: first letters of the and guard
con = against, as in pros and cons

annotation.surface: Guerrillas fighting their way against the leaders held in a guardhouse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guard house' reads as one building, but house is the verb: the two initials house CON.
annotation.definitionFit: The Vietcong were the communist guerrillas of the Vietnam War.

entries.clue: Maths book concealing fiddle on test (12)

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so the book holds the other letters within it

blocks.note: a tome is a large book
to rig is to fiddle a result

annotation.surface: A maths textbook hiding a cheat for an exam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maths book' looks like a single textbook, but the definition stops at Maths and the book is only wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the study of triangles and angles is one branch of maths.

entries.clue: Discarded bit of fruit upset bears when hibernating (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, set upside down: read upwards
in a down clue, LEEP carries AS on top

blocks.note: the peel is the part thrown away

annotation.surface: Bears in winter, dozing among the fruit scraps they have knocked over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bears' is a verb, not animals, though the surface uses the animals to make hibernating fit.
annotation.definitionFit: Hibernation is a long winter sleep, so the adjective fits as a near synonym.

entries.clue: Fiat 500 king much appreciated when taken in it (6)

indicators.note: K and TA are taken inside IT

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thank you

annotation.surface: A Fiat 500 hatchback that a king adores and drives around.
annotation.walkthrough: The Fiat 500 is a small car, which welds '500' to 'Fiat'; fiat here is a decree.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms: both words, Latin and German borrowings, name a decree imposed by authority.

entries.clue: Have larks avoided bitter berries? (3,6)

blocks.note: to cut someone or something is to avoid it
capers are sharp-tasting pickled buds and berries

annotation.surface: Birds steering clear of sour berries.
annotation.walkthrough: Larks look like birds eating berries, but 'have larks' means have fun.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for an idiom: a caper is a playful leap, and larks are pranks, both meaning to frolic.

entries.clue: What flipping idiot has bagged barbecue leftovers? (5)

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the word is read backwards
to bag something is to put it in a bag, so one word holds the other

annotation.surface: An exasperated question about what some fool has pocketed from the barbecue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word; it is the reversal of EH.
annotation.definitionFit: Ashes are what is left once a barbecue burns out.

entries.clue: Issue of immigrants aboard dinghies insoluble, on reflection (5)

indicators.note: the answer is carried inside the words
reflected: read backwards

annotation.surface: The migrant crossing in small boats described as an intractable problem.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'issue' as a political problem; here it means offspring.
annotation.definitionFit: The Nisei are American-born children of Japanese immigrants.

entries.clue: Choice for suit perhaps set, hearts (5)

blocks.note: to clot is to set solid

annotation.surface: A card player picking a suit, perhaps hearts.
annotation.walkthrough: The cards in the surface mislead: the suit is clothing, and cloth is chosen for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by 'perhaps': picking the material is one choice made for a tailored suit.

entries.clue: Lowest in society played bingo in case (9)

indicators.note: the letters are played about with

annotation.surface: The poorest people in society played bingo, just in case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In case' looks like a container instruction, but it is simply LEST.
annotation.definitionFit: Ignoblest means lowest in rank, humblest.

entries.clue: Newspaper customer possibly wanting substance rather than ad catalogue (8)

indicators.note: READER wants GIST in its middle
choosing one thing rather than another means swapping it in, so the new letters take the old ones' place

blocks.note: a reader is one kind of newspaper customer
the gist is the substance of something
AD in READER is swapped out

annotation.surface: A newspaper buyer who would prefer real content to advertisements.
annotation.walkthrough: The ad complaint in the surface is literal: the letters AD come out of READER.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are official lists recording entries.

entries.clue: Slide down deep hole? Never mind (4,2)

blocks.note: to ski is to slide down a slope
a pit is a deep hole

annotation.surface: Someone thinking of skiing into a crevasse, then dropping the idea.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the break between wordplay and definition.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Skip it' and 'never mind' both dismiss a subject.
